name: Crunch and sit-up
pattern: Trunk flexion: the ribs curl toward the pelvis. A crunch lifts only the shoulder blades; a sit-up keeps going until the trunk is upright.
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat about hip width.
Hands across your chest or fingertips lightly behind your ears.
Low back in its natural curve, not pressed hard into the floor.

steps.text: Breathe out and curl your ribs toward your hips until your shoulder blades leave the floor.
Pause for a moment, chin about a fist from your chest.
Uncurl slowly, one part of the spine at a time, until your shoulders touch down.

cues.cue: Ribs to hips: curl, don't hinge.
cues.why: Curling the trunk works the abs; swinging up from the hips shifts work to the hip flexors and loads the low back more.

cues.cue: Lift just your shoulder blades for a crunch.
cues.why: The curl-up challenges the abs with much less low-back compression than a full sit-up.

cues.cue: Keep a fist between chin and chest, hands don't pull.
cues.why: Pulling on the head bends the neck instead of the trunk.

cues.cue: Feet free, not hooked under a pad, for crunches.
cues.why: Anchored feet let the hip flexors take over the lift.

cues.cue: Lower slowly, no bounce off the floor.
cues.why: Control keeps the abs working through the whole range.

breathing: Breathe out as you curl up, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Curl in about 1 second, hold 1, lower in 2.

mistakes.name: Pulling the head
mistakes.looks: Hands yank the head forward and the chin hits the chest.
mistakes.fix: Hands light behind the ears or across the chest; look at the ceiling.
mistakes.why: The neck bends while the trunk barely moves.

mistakes.name: Swinging up from the hips
mistakes.looks: The back stays flat or arched and the whole trunk hinges up at the hips.
mistakes.fix: Curl the ribs down first; free the feet.
mistakes.why: Hip flexors (psoas, iliacus) take the load and press on the low back.

mistakes.name: Throwing the arms
mistakes.looks: Arms fling forward to throw the body up.
mistakes.fix: Arms across the chest; move slower.
mistakes.why: Momentum, not the abs, does the lift.

safety: Low back pain: choose curl-ups over full sit-ups; they load the spine less.
Neck strain: rest your head in your hands or on a towel between reps.
Pregnancy (later stages) or abdominal separation: ask your clinician before lying-flat crunches.

variants.change: Curling on a ball raises abdominal activity compared with the floor.
Head lower than feet: harder, more hip flexor work.
Load held on the chest is easiest; held overhead or pressed up is harder.
Turning one shoulder toward the opposite knee adds oblique work.
Full sit-up: about twice the trunk range and more hip flexor and low-back load than a crunch.

easier: curl-up with hands under the low back

subtypes.name: Sit-up
subtypes.change: The trunk keeps rising to upright; hips flex a lot.

subtypes.name: Kneeling or standing cable crunch
subtypes.change: Kneel facing away from the cable, rope by your head; curl the ribs toward the hips while the hips stay still.

subtypes.name: Seated crunch machine
subtypes.change: Seated, chest or hands on the pads; curl down against the weight.

metrics.label: Trunk lift
metrics.good: -65 to -55 at the top of a crunch (shoulder blades just off the floor)

motion.basis: All angles are estimates from the described technique (shoulder blades clear the floor at about 30 degrees of trunk lift). Upper-trunk curl is shown with the trunk key; the convention has no thoracic key. Twisting variants need trunk rotation, which the convention lacks.
